{{Quote|Bal'demnic is that important?''"<br />"''A hunch.|Larsh Hill and Hego Damask|<ref name="dp" />}}
'''Bal'demnic''' was an [[Ocean/Legends|ocean]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] adorned with rocky tropical islands in the [[Bak'rofsen system]] of the [[Auril sector/Legends|Auril sector]], located within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. The hostility of its [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] [[Kon'me]] [[Species/Legends|species]], together with its extremely harsh climate, discouraged most people from ever visiting the planet, despite the beauty of its giant rock cliffs, pristine beaches, and vast [[Color/Legends|azure]] oceans. It was mostly of interest to [[Cartographer/Legends|cartographers]], [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]], and [[Fishing/Legends|fisherfolk]], until knowledge of the planet's rich deposits of [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]] ore fell into the hands of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] [[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]] and [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]].

After Plagueis killed his [[Sith Master/Legends|master]] Tenebrous on the planet, and later acquired [[Mining/Legends|mining]] rights to a large portion of the main continent, Bal'demnic did not figure into pan-[[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Politics/Legends|politics]] until the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] moved in to invade and mine Bal'demnic of its cortosis to bolster their own war effort. However, the Kon'me eventually [[Battle of Bal'demnic|rose up]] against the invaders, just as they were about to be liberated by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. As a result, the natives drove off both the Republic and the Confederacy, although the former maintained a significant [[Navy/Legends|naval]] presence in the [[Star system/Legends|system]] following the battle.

==Description==
{{Quote|The galactic economy is a hypercomplex system, full of unexpected movements and ill-discerned effects, where the flutter of a pigeon on Trantor may create a typhoon on Bal'demnic.|The Golden Emperor of Prekaz|<ref name="ttsp">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/praji/20090205.html|text=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji|int=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji}}</ref>}}
Located in the [[Bak'rofsen system]], which was in turn found within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]' [[Auril sector/Legends|Auril sector]], Bal'demnic was considered a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of stark yet rugged beauty. Mostly covered by [[Ocean/Legends|ocean]], the world was pockmarked with small tropical beach islands, a small primary continent, and a northern polar ice cap. To an unwitting observer, the planet was an aesthetic paradise. Vast azure oceans glistened in the sun, crashing white on the shorelines of land masses tiny and large. High cliffs and narrow rock formations towered through the white mists of the rough seas. Pristine beaches of both white and black sands rested at the bottom of gargantuan canyons.<ref name="dp" />

The planet's scorching climate kept any would-be holiday maker well away, however. Bal'demnic held a noxious atmosphere, and seismic events often rocked the planet and changed the landscape. [[Hawk-bat/Legends|Hawk-bats]] took shelter in crystalline caves often found just below the coastal rocky surface. Bloodthirsty [[Insect/Legends|insects]] flew in swarms along the dry treeless terrain. Great winds whistled through the cliffs, and heavy rains surged in the wet seasons of the planet's long [[Standard year/Legends|year]].<ref name="dp" />

The native Kon'me had razed much of the planet's forests for building materials and firewood, leaving only inaccessible vegetation found on steep sided gorge walls. The planet's primary city contained [[Kon'meas Spaceport]], perched at the top of high cliffs overlooking the ocean. Shorelines were dotted with beachside dwellings, the high class living in glistening bubble-like structures embedded within the high cliffs. The low class fashioned simple thatched huts on the beaches.<ref name="dp" />

Late in the planet's history, veins of rich [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]] ore were discovered in the planet's surface&mdash;a property that made Bal'demnic a point of contention during the pan-[[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="db" />

==History==
===Murder of a Sith Master===
{{Quote|Darth Bane's early years. Carrying on the ancestral business, as it were.''"<br />"''What more appropriate way for us to close the circle than by mimicking the Sith'ari's seminal efforts. We weave ourselves into the warp and weft of the tapestry he created.|Darth Plagueis and Darth Tenebrous|<ref name="dp" />}}
In [[67 BBY/Legends|67 BBY]], [[Subtext Mining]] provided [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]] with secret intelligence revealing large deposits of [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]] ore within the planet's crust. Tenebrous acted on the new information personally, traveling to Bal'demnic with his apprentice, [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]]. Tenebrous ascribed special significance to the mission, believing that two Sith Lords mining cortosis at the apex of the [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]] era amounted to the "closing of a circle," a circle that had began with [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], starting on the path toward darkness in the [[Apatros/Legends|Apatros]] cortosis mines a millennium earlier.<ref name="dp" />

[[File:Darth_Plagueis.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Darth Plagueis stands triumphant in a cavern on Bal'demnic after killing his master.]]
In a crystalline cave, Tenebrous commanded Subtext's [[M-2 mining probe droid]] to verify the secret mining survey team's claims. During the process, the M-2 unit ceased taking orders from the Sith Lord, and proceeded to drill in the direction of a highly combustible pocket of [[lethane]] gas. Tenebrous sensed great danger and fled the cave with his apprentice. Before they were able to reach the surface, the Sith Lords were overcome by the large explosion caused by the M-2 unit's breach of the lethane pocket. The surrounding cavern ceiling collapsed, and both Master and Apprentice used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to prevent large slabs of rock falling on them and their ship.<ref name="dp" />

With Tenebrous distracted, Plagueis realized that the fear his Master had sensed earlier was his own death - at his apprentice's hands. With the Force, Plagueis sent the levitated slabs crashing down on Tenebrous, crushing him almost to death, and damaging his ship. After a brief exchange of words, Plagueis snapped his Master's neck. Tenebrous' remains would be undisturbed for decades, possibly centuries, after his death.<ref name="dp" />

Over a long sleepless night, Plagueis traveled on foot utilizing a [[Force speed/Legends|Force speed]] technique to cover hundreds of kilometers to [[Kon'meas Spaceport]]. There he stowed aboard the ''[[Woebegone]]'', whose crew he killed whilst in transit, and took the ship to [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]].<ref name="dp" />

===A most valuable resource===
{{Quote|I want you to familiarize yourself with a world called Bal'demnic. Once you have, you're to acquire mining rights for the entire northeast peninsula of the principle landmass. Purchase as much property as you can.|Hego Damask, to Larsh Hill|<ref name="dp" />}}
On his return to Muunilinst, Plagueis entrusted [[Larsh Hill]] to purchase large amounts of Bal'demnic land and acquire mining rights for the cortosis-addled mainland.<ref name="dp" />

Despite killing his master, Plagueis sought to avenge Tenebrous' betrayal at the hands of Subtext Mining. Under the Sith Lord's deathly interrogation, the [[Gossam/Legends|Gossam]] owners of Subtext revealed to Plagueis unprecedented natural reserves of [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]] on the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. In essence, the Sith duo's mining survey on Bal'demnic revealed a far greater discovery that would shape the future of the galaxy--Darth Plagueis meeting young [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="dp" />

At some point over the next two decades, a secret mining operation on Bal'demnic was established. Some of the processed ore was used in the manufacture of [[Cortosis shield/Legends|cortosis shields]]. [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] supplied a shield to the [[Yinchorri/Legends|Yinchorri]], to be used [[Raid on the Jedi Temple (Yinchorri Uprising)|against the Jedi]] during the [[Yinchorri Uprising]] of [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]]. The shield from Bal'demnic's ore proved to be most effective, factoring into the deaths of two Jedi during the raid: [[Jude Rozess]] and [[Tieren Nie-Tan]].<ref name="dp" />

===The battle for cortosis===
During the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]], the Confederacy saw the occupation of Bal'demnic and its cortosis as vital to the war effort.<ref name="db" /> Fitting in with their campaign to direct Republic forces away from the Core, the Confederacy descended upon the ocean world during the third [[19 BBY/Legends|year]] of the Clone Wars.<ref name="atlas" /> The invading force ordered the native Kon'me to either allow cortosis [[Mining/Legends|mining]] operations to begin, or be destroyed. The upper-class cliff-dwelling Kon'me consented to Confederate occupation, and allowed the operations to begin. In spite of this, the beachfront Kon'me were outraged, and began to develop small pockets of resistance against the invaders.<ref name="db" />

[[File:WTS-CloneWarsPlanet.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Battle of Bal'demnic.]]
Confederacy transmissions relevant to the Bal'demnic situation were eventually intercepted by the Republic. [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] realized the potential danger of a Confederate hold on Bal'demnic's cortosis reserves&mdash;as a result, the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] dispatched a task force led by Jedi Knights [[Halagad Ventor]] and [[Sha Koon]] to investigate and sabotage the Confederate operation. The Republic force, however, found Bal'demnic in chaos. The Kon'me had [[Battle of Bal'demnic|risen up]] and cast off the yoke of Confederate rule, using high-tech weaponry that had been [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggled]] to them by war profiteers.<ref name="db" /> With mounted weaponry in their bubble-like cliff dwellings, the Kon'me were pitted against the combined [[Armor/Legends|armor]] of the Confederate [[Droid/Legends|droids]]. The Confederacy, in turn, dispatched [[OG-9 homing spider droid/Legends|OG-9 homing spider droids]] to overrun the Kon'me positions.<ref name="cw">{{CW|22}}</ref> When Ventor and Koon's [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] landed, the situation only escalated, resulting in the natives firing on all offworlders, regardless of affiliation. Due to the unusual and unfamiliar island terrain, both the Confederate and Republic forces retreated. With the Confederacy no longer able to harvest the cortosis, the Republic left an [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] above Bal'demnic to dissuade any further incursions from their adversaries.<ref name="db" />

The planet was mentioned by the [[Golden Emperor of Prekaz]], in his commentary on the state of the galactic economy. The Emperor's quote was later included as an epigraph in [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Gabrel Treon]] writings on [[House Praji/Legends|House Praji]] for the [[Byblos Journal of Historical Science]], entitled "[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes]]."<ref name="ttsp" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|The indegenes will be troublesome to negotiate with, but I'm confident they can be persuaded.|Hego Damask, to Larsh Hill|<ref name="dp" />}}
[[File:Konme-CWChapter22.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Kon'me defend Bal'demnic from the Confederacy of Independent Systems.]]
{{Main|Kon'me}}
The reptilian Kon'me were the only known [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to Bal'demnic. Their disposition was notorious offworld for being abrasive and isolationist, and they had a class-structure illustrated by location of residence. For instance, the upper-class Kon'me resided in more opulent structures within the beachside cliff walls than their lower-class counterparts. The cliff-dwelling Kon'me made planetary decisions, such as the acceptance of a Confederate occupation during the Clone Wars, whereas the lower-class was destined to bear the brunt of such decisions. As a result, a rift grew between the two classes during the war, with the beach-dwellers establishing a resistance against the Confederates that their upper-class counterparts had welcomed.<ref name="db" />

Many offworlders visited Bal'demnic for trading purposes; mostly [[Alien/Legends|non-Humans]] from neighboring star systems, [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]], the far reaches of the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] and some hailing from as far as the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="dp" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I really wanted to come up with a name that sounded both unique and believable; hopefully I succeeded.|Arthur Papadam|<ref name="blog">{{Blog|arfmaul|7|The Making of Bal'demnic: The Island Planet}}</ref>}}
Bal'demnic first appeared in "[[Chapter 22 (Star Wars: Clone Wars)|Chapter 22]]," an episode of ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]''. It was shown fleetingly in a montage of [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] invasions across the galaxy. It was later named, and elaborated on by [[Arthur Papadam]], under the pseudonym "Arf Maul", through [[StarWars.com]]'s [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature, "[[What's The Story?]]" Papadam derived the name "Bal'demnic" from the word "condemn," while also making it similar to "demonic," suggesting that the planet's inhabitants were not as innocent as they might have appeared. The first syllable, "Bal," was derived from one of Papadam's friend's nicknames: "B'daniel." In his entry, Papadam also connected the planet to various other disparate elements from the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]], including Halagad Ventor from [[West End Games]]' ''[[Domain of Evil]]'' adventure supplement, and Sha Koon from [[Star Wars: The Stark Hyperspace War|''The Stark Hyperspace War'']], an arc from the [[Star Wars: Republic|''Star Wars'']] comic line. In addition to this, Papadam placed Bal'demnic in the Auril sector as he wished to reference the planet [[Courkrus|Khuiumin IV]], as a way of paying homage to one of his favorite ''[[Star Wars]]'' games, [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']]. Papadam's placement stemmed from the belief (later disproved in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'') that Khuiumin was also located in the Auril sector; however, he cut his reference to Khuiumin from the final entry.<ref name="blog" />

Following that, the planet received its own entries in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' and [[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 2|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 2]] in [[2008]]. The planet also gained brief attention from sources such as [[2009]]'s article ''[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji]]'' by [[Nathan O'Keefe]] and the same year's ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]]. The Atlas confirmed that the Battle of Bal'demnic occurred during the third year of the Clone Wars, and provided the coordinates for Bal'demnic on the galactic map.

Bal'demnic was referenced by [[Abel G. Peña]] in his final draft of ''[[Underworld Appendix: Swoops, Spice, and Wretched Rogues]]'', but was cut out of the final release.<ref name="tfn">{{JCFCite|url=posts/24845428|board=Literature|thread=Insider 89: "Underworld: A Galaxy of Scum and Villainy" by Abel, Ryan, and Joe|user=Halagad_Ventor|date=2006-08-29|time=2:05 PM}}</ref>

Papadam's writings were largely elaborated upon in the [[2012]] novel [[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']] by [[James Luceno]], and the supplemental article ''[[The Tenebrous Way]]'' by [[Matthew Stover]] and ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]]. Luceno established Bal'demnic as the location of the death of [[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]] at the hands of his apprentice, [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]]. The planet's geography and history were greatly expanded on in Luceno's novel, also setting in motion events that led to the Battle of Bal'demnic during the Clone Wars.

Later that year, Bal'demnic was included in illustrations of the galactic map for the first time by [[Modi]] in ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''. Here, Bal'demnic is shown to be in the far top-right corner of grid coordinate R7, in very close proximity to [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], [[Belderone/Legends|Belderone]] and [[Trogan/Legends|Trogan]].
